reason: A is the stronger proposal because an external silicide coating is a well-established, physically plausible route to supply a concentrated scale-forming element without altering the RHEA bulk, and it specifies a controlled comparison with measurable oxidation and scale outcomes. Its citation supports only the oxidation limitation—not the coating efficacy—and its broad conditions and unsupported 50% target need refinement, but B is less grounded because 5–10 wt% Al does not reliably guarantee selective, continuous external alumina formation in a multicomponent refractory alloy.
